deadline.value: Fall admission and priority graduate assistantship deadline is February 1, 2027.
deadline.quote: All application materials must be received by February 1 for fall admission consideration.

also.quote: The deadline for receipt of application materials for admission into the EES program is February 1.

gre_general.value: Not stated as required on the Earth and Ecosystem Science Ph.D. admission pages or Graduate Bulletin.

gre_subject.value: ETS offers no GRE Subject Test in Earth or Environmental Sciences (Subject Tests exist only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants must contact a faculty member before applying and secure sponsorship from a participating faculty advisor prepared to support their research.
supervisor.quote: Before applying, you must contact a faculty member whose research aligns with your interests. Admission requires sponsorship by a participating faculty advisor who is prepared to support your research.

funding.value: Admitted EES Ph.D. students must have financial support in the form of a teaching or research assistantship (stipend and tuition waiver) in place; most EES Ph.D. students are funded via RAs/TAs.
funding.quote: Students admitted for a doctoral degree in EES must have a faculty mentor approved and financial support in the form of a teaching or research assistantship in place.

also.quote: Most admitted students to the Ph.D. and thesis-based (Plan A) M.S. program receive financial support through a combination of research and teaching assistantships.

entry_route.value: Bachelor of Science (B.S.) or Master of Science (M.S.) degree in chemistry, biology, engineering, geology, geography, atmospheric science, or a related science (minimum 3.0 GPA).
entry_route.quote: Candidates are expected to hold a Bachelor of Science (B.S.) or Master of Science (M.S.) degree in chemistry, biology, engineering, geology, geography, atmospheric science, or other relevant areas of science.

notes: 60-credit-hour multidisciplinary Ph.D. spanning aquatic and terrestrial ecosystems, Great Lakes systems, climate, environmental engineering, and geology.
name: Ph.D. in Earth and Ecosystem Science
